title: The Zenith Deep Where Stone Learns the Sky

features.name: the standing witness
features.desc-on-touch: A needle of stone worn by centuries of altitude and wind; you read its surfaces and find them aligned to three different weather systems at once—contradicting forecasts, all of them true.

features.name: the sky-pool
features.desc-on-touch: Water cupped in stone, so still it becomes a window. When you look, you see not the sky above but the sky the stone remembers—different clouds, a different year.

features.name: the altitude-scar
features.desc-on-touch: A groove in the ridge where lightning has chosen the same path seven times. The groove hums at particular wind speeds, and the archive has learned to read the pitch as a record of how many times the sky changed its mind here.

features.name: the cairn-that-grows-backward
features.desc-on-touch: Stones are slowly moving downhill, rearranging themselves. Climbers who pass it twice find their route markers in a different order—the mountain is learning to erase its own paths.

features.name: the breath-thin shelter
features.desc-on-touch: A crease in the rock where altitude once broke someone's descent. The stone still holds the shape of a hand's grip, and on certain winds, you hear a breath drawn slowly inward.

inscription: stone learns only when it stops arguing with the sky

file.name: HighCountry_WindPatterns_Unverified_2013-2019.wav
file.note: Audio recordings of sustained wind tones from various altitudes; the corruption has layered three incompatible stations' data—now it plays like a chord only stone could sing.

reverie.title: REVERIE — high-ridge noon, stone-learning
narr: You stand at the zenith and she kneels by the pool,
tracing fingers on water that will not move.
The stone around you both holds its breath.
'It learns slower than we do,' she says—but her voice
carries like wind that's only now remembering its shape.
